niche_preference_profile: This user most consistently prefers interfaces with strong visual hierarchy, lower clutter, and either light neutral surfaces with soft purple accents or deep navy dark themes with richer contrast. They repeatedly favor layouts that feel open, focused, and structured, with fewer competing panels, clearer section separation, and content emphasized over chrome. They like rounded components, prominent and clearly prioritized actions, concise but explicit copy, and controls that are labeled or otherwise easy to interpret. In many cases they prefer compact but efficient information presentation, as long as the screen remains organized and visually calm.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers light neutral backgrounds with soft purple accents in many product and form-like screens, and prefers deep navy/blue-black dark themes over flatter charcoal or mixed dark treatments when dark UI is used. Generally rejects harsher blue accents, lower-contrast dark themes, and overly heavy high-contrast dark styling.
Prefers open spacing, fewer crowded elements, and reduced visual clutter. Repeatedly chooses screens with more breathing room, less stacked UI, and fewer overlays or decorative layers.

Prefers clear hierarchy with one dominant focal area, strong section separation, and content-first layouts. Likes screens where code, primary cards, or key content clearly dominate instead of competing with headers, toolbars, metrics, or multiple panels.

Prefers visible, prominent, and clearly prioritized actions, especially strong primary CTAs supported by secondary actions. Favors labeled buttons and balanced action hierarchy over hidden, icon-only, disabled-looking, or weakly emphasized controls.

Prefers information that is efficiently organized and scannable: compact layouts, structured rows or grids, visible labels, and richer useful content when it is clearly arranged. Rejects both sparse under-informative screens and dense unstructured groupings.

Prefers lighter, subtler container treatments such as single primary cards, translucent floating panels, flatter minimalist sections, or even no enclosing card at all for simple states. Dislikes heavy opaque overlays, too many competing cards, and bulky container chrome.
Prefers softer, more rounded cards, buttons, and icon shapes, along with an overall polished and approachable visual tone rather than sharper rectangular or harsher component styling.
